analysis:
All changes in this batch are CI and workflow plumbing. None touches the provider, native runtime, coordinator contract, keys, attestation, the prefix cache (T-041) or any other asset in the canonical model.

- bedrock-smoke.yml line 9: the runner label changes from a Blacksmith runner to ubuntu-24.04. Permissions (contents: read, id-token: write), the master-only guard, the pinned actions and the role-assumption step are unchanged. The AWS trust is based on OIDC claims, not the runner pool, so I found no new exposure. The IAM role trust policy was not supplied.
- ci-dev-hourly.yml is removed. This drops the actions: write dispatcher and the hourly-failures issue writer, which reduces privilege surface. The trade-off is less frequent full-tree CI, which is a testing-cadence matter and not a security regression.
- ci-dev.yml (head lines 12-83): PR runs are now opt-in through the labeled event with run-ci or run-gpu-ci. Only users with triage or write access can apply labels. The unlabel job has issues and pull-requests write, using github.token, and only runs a fixed DELETE on a constant label path. PR_NUMBER comes from the event payload and is passed as an env var, so there is no script injection. The job runs no PR code. Concurrency groups isolate unrelated labels. The tests job still has contents: read only and no secrets.
- ci-master.yml: only metadata and a truncated patch excerpt were supplied. The visible hunks add a labeled trigger, a similar concurrency group and an unlabel job, which looks analogous to ci-dev.yml. The remainder was not visible, so I could not confirm that job's permissions.
- test-threat-model-review.py: the tests assert that threat-model-review.yml uses a labeled trigger, gates on run-threat-model, uses ubuntu-24.04, and keeps concurrency at job level. The workflow file itself is not in this batch. Its secret-bearing pull_request_target handling and trusted-scanner and base-context separation (asserted at lines 741-779 of the test) need confirmation in the workflow diff.

No finding is supported by the supplied evidence. The open items are the unseen threat-model-review.yml and the full ci-master.yml unlabel and permission changes.
